cpu.locator: DESCRIPTION CPU user/idle/iowait fields, rendered lines24–57
cpu.reviewed_definition: User time is execution in user mode, so it includes client programs but not their kernel time. Idle is time in the idle task. I/O wait tracks waiting for I/O, but its per-CPU accounting is unreliable and can decrease. It cannot independently identify storage as the sole bottleneck.
cpu.primary_excerpt:
user: normal processes executing in user mode
idle: twiddling thumbs
iowait: In a word, iowait stands for waiting for I/O to complete. But there are several problems:
CPU will not wait for I/O to complete, iowait is the time that a task is waiting for I/O to complete. When CPU goes into idle state for outstanding task I/O, another task will be scheduled on this CPU.
In a multi-core CPU, the task waiting for I/O to complete is not running on any CPU, so the iowait of each CPU is difficult to calculate.
The value of iowait field in /proc/stat will decrease in certain conditions.
So, the iowait is not reliable by reading from /proc/stat.

memory.quote: An estimate of how much memory is available
memory.reviewed_definition: MemTotal is usable physical RAM after reserved memory and kernel code. MemAvailable estimates capacity for new applications without swapping and includes reclaimable caches, while accounting for cache that must stay. Cached includes page cache and tmpfs/shared memory; it is not a promise that every cached byte is immediately reclaimable. Buffers is temporary storage for raw disk blocks.
memory.primary_excerpt:
MemTotal
Total usable RAM (i.e. physical RAM minus a few reserved bits and the kernel binary code)
MemAvailable
An estimate of how much memory is available for starting new applications, without swapping. Calculated from MemFree, SReclaimable, the size of the file LRU lists, and the low watermarks in each zone. The estimate takes into account that the system needs some page cache to function well, and that not all reclaimable slab will be reclaimable, due to items being in use. The impact of those factors will vary from system to system.
Buffers
Relatively temporary storage for raw disk blocks shouldn’t get tremendously large (20MB or so)
Cached
In-memory cache for files read from the disk (the pagecache) as well as tmpfs & shmem. Doesn’t include SwapCached.
Unevictable
Memory allocated for userspace which cannot be reclaimed, such as mlocked pages, ramfs backing pages, secret memfd pages etc.

io.quote: This field increases so long as field 9 is nonzero.
io.reviewed_definition: The kernel reports completed read/write operations, transferred sectors and time with I/O active. Rates derive from changes over elapsed time: IOPS means operations per second and throughput means transferred bytes per second. Busy-time accounting has known limitations, especially with concurrent I/O; it does not measure a percentage of maximum storage performance.
io.primary_excerpt:
Field 1 -- # of reads completed (unsigned long)
This is the total number of reads completed successfully.
Field 3 -- # of sectors read (unsigned long)
This is the total number of sectors read successfully.
Field 5 -- # of writes completed (unsigned long)
This is the total number of writes completed successfully.
Field 7 -- # of sectors written (unsigned long)
This is the total number of sectors written successfully.
Field 10 -- # of milliseconds spent doing I/Os (unsigned int)
This field increases so long as field 9 is nonzero.
Since 5.0 this field counts jiffies when at least one request was started or completed. If request runs more than 2 jiffies then some I/O time might be not accounted in case of concurrent requests.
